notes: RPA (Romanized Popular Alphabet, Smalley/Barney/Bertrais 1953). Monosyllabic/tonal: no lexical word stress is orthographically predictable, so no `stress` block is set (docs/quality_tiers.md stress exemption for tonal monosyllabic languages, cf. Vietnamese and Yoruba specs). WORD-FINAL CONSONANT LETTERS MARK TONE, NOT CODAS: every RPA syllable is (onset)(rhyme), and the seven letters b/j/v/s/g/m/d that can follow the rhyme spell one of eight tones rather than a coda consonant (Smalley 1976; Ratliff 2010 'Hmong-Mien Language History' ch.4). Tone is written: the seven tone letters resolve to the Chao pitch mark they spell (b=˥, j=˥˧, v=˧˦, s=˩, g=˧˩̤, m=˩̰, d=˧́ — Smalley 1976; Ratliff 2010 ch.4), and an unmarked syllable carries the mid tone ˧ by default (`allophone_rules MWW_MID_UNSPELLED_*`, the same bake-then-strip mechanism the ycl spec uses: every rime nucleus's default candidate is the vowel plus ˧, and that ˧ is stripped back out whenever one of the seven marked tone letters follows and spells the real tone instead). ⟨b/j/g⟩ never spell an onset consonant, so they carry their tone mark unconditionally; ⟨s/m/v/d⟩ are homographs of onset consonants (s=/ʂ/ retroflex fricative, m=/m/, v=/v/, d=/d/), so `positional_graphemes: after_vowel` is what carries their tone mark, since Hmong has no codas and these letters are onsets only word/syllable-initially. The eighth tone (-d, a raised-mid tone restricted to recent Chinese loanwords, Ratliff 2010:34) is modelled the same way though it does not occur in the registered gold. Distinctive onset inventory verified directly against the WikiPron mww_latn_broad.tsv gold (492 rows): plain vs. aspirated vs. prenasalized vs. prenasalized-aspirated series across bilabial/dental/palatal/velar/uvular places, plus voiceless sonorants (hl/hm/hn/hny) and the lateral-release series (pl/ml/plh/npl/nplh). ⟨s⟩=/ʂ/ (retroflex) and ⟨x⟩=/s/ (dental) is the traditional RPA assignment (reversed from the letters' IPA values), confirmed by the gold. Nasalized vowels ⟨ee⟩=/ẽ/, ⟨oo⟩=/ɒ̃/; oral ⟨o⟩=/ɒ/ (open back rounded, not /ɔ/). Diphthongs ⟨ai⟩, ⟨au⟩, ⟨aw⟩, ⟨ia⟩, ⟨ua⟩ are single nuclei (AGENTS.md #2 test 2) with a non-syllabic offglide, matching the gold's narrow transcription (a i̯, a u̯, a ɨ̯, i ə̯, u ə̯). ⟨w⟩ alone is the central vowel /ɨ/, not a labialization mark: no genuine Cw labialized-consonant cluster is attested in the gold (every apparent Cw sequence resolves to onset+/ɨ/, e.g. kws=k+ɨ+s(tone)). ⟨s/m/v/d⟩ additionally carry an `intervocalic` override restoring the plain onset consonant: intervocalic position is checked before after_vowel in the engine's resolution order, so it correctly re-disambiguates a loanword CVCV sequence (⟨amelika⟩: intervocalic ⟨m⟩ stays /m/, not silent-tone) from a genuine tone-letter followed by the next syllable's onset (⟨misnisxaustas⟩: each medial ⟨s⟩ is after a vowel but before a CONSONANT, so it still resolves to the silent tone slot). `vowel_graphemes: ["w"]` declares ⟨w⟩ a vowel letter, overriding the engine's closed Latin vowel-letter inventory (which otherwise treats ⟨w⟩ as a consonant regardless of IPA, as it must for Czech syllabic ⟨r⟩ and English ⟨y⟩; see orthography2ipa/vowels.py), so the after_vowel/intervocalic positional checks above correctly fire when the rhyme is bare ⟨w⟩ (⟨tswv⟩, ⟨kws⟩, ⟨txwm⟩) and the following tone letter is silenced instead of surfacing as a spurious consonant.
